subject: Urgent: short-notice fallback bridge patch and mitigation steps
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: ops@acme-corp.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: short-notice fallback bridge patch and mitigation steps

Hi Alice / Acme Ops team,

Quick update — we observed an increasing rate of prefix-eviction errors on a small subset of inference hosts handling short-lived chats (10–30 token bursts). This is causing latency spikes and a small number of 5xxs for routed hosted traffic in us-west-2. We are issuing a targeted, short-notice fallback "bridge" patch that switches impacted model variants to a conservative KV-eviction policy and disables speculative prefetch for the next 45 minutes while we validate.

Impact: a small portion of requests may see slightly higher mean latency (+40–70ms) but should avoid the spikes and errors. No data loss expected.

Requested action for Acme: if you have long-running streaming sessions, please notify us if you cannot tolerate ~50–80ms additional p99 latency for up to 45m. Otherwise no immediate action required; patch is designed as graceful fallback.

We are attaching the patch and a short rollback runbook for your on-call. Our status page will be updated.

Attachments: bridge-patch-1.2.patch, runbook-quick-rollback.pdf

I will post progress updates here.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Alice Tan <alice.tan@acme-corp.com>

Cc: ops@acme-corp.com
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: short-notice fallback bridge patch and mitigation steps

Thanks Naomi — quick clarifying questions:

1) Can you confirm which model flavors and route IDs will be switched to conservative eviction? We need to know whether our batch-oriented pipelines (route: acme-embed-batch) are included.
2) Is there any expected change to token accounting / billing during the fallback window?
3) If we apply the patch from our side, are there extra steps we must run to rehydrate caches?

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: short-notice fallback bridge patch and mitigation steps

Alice — good questions, answers below: 

1) Affected model flavors: rwd-1.3 (chat-variant) and rwd-1.3-quantized variants. Route IDs targeted: user-chat-1, user-chat-1-highprio. Batch routes such as acme-embed-batch are NOT part of the rollback; they will remain on standard policy.

2) Token accounting: no change to billing model. There may be a negligible rounding difference if requests take an extra token due to conservative prefetch being disabled, but nothing we will bill differently.

3) If you choose to apply the patch from your side (we are pushing it from our control plane by default for hosted customers), please run the rehydrate command in the attached runbook once the patch is applied: ./rehydrate-cache --routes user-chat-1,user-chat-1-highprio. That will warm the prefix cache; it is recommended but not required.

We have kicked the patch to the affected pools at 09:30 PDT. Expected validation window: 30–45m. We will post telemetry summary once validation completes.

Status link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-09-17-bridge
Ticket: INC-4472

—Naomi

Team — forwarding the thread for visibility. Short internal notes:

- Marcus: please watch the canary pool telemetry (pool: us-west-2-canary-3). Increase sampling if p99 remains noisy after 20m.
- Monica: coordinate with SLAs/CS for any accounts that request exceptions; Acme is OK but flag any escalation tickets.
- If the rollback window extends >60m we will prepare an automated revert plan (INC-4472).

Thanks Naomi — confirm we applied the bridge patch at 09:36 PDT yesterday via your control-plane push. We followed your runbook and ran the rehydrate step; p99 latency normalized after ~12m and we saw no further 5xxs. We did observe a small increase in mean latency for our streaming tests (~60ms) but that was within our tolerance.

Please keep me posted on the postmortem / root-cause analysis and long-term mitigation timeline. We will keep INC-4472 open on our side.
